notes:
Summary: Proxima Knowledge Labs is evaluating a RAG/enterprise search stack to surface financial documents, research notes, and compliance artifacts to analysts with sub-200ms query latency and high precision. They already have ~250M raw documents and estimate 350M - 500M vectors after chunking.

Key quotes: "Need predictable unit economics — we can’t accept hidden per-query spikes." — Head of ML Ops.

Technical requirements / preferences (from calls):
- Indexing scale: target 350M vectors initially, plan to grow to ~1B within 12–18 months.
- Throughput target: sustain 150–300 QPS during batch windows; baseline 50 QPS for interactive search.
- Latency target: P95 < 120ms, P99 < 250ms for top-k vector retrieval; end-to-end rerank (cross-encoder on top 50 candidates) P99 < 600ms.
- Cost sensitivity: target cost per interactive query <$0.005 (emb+ann+rerank amortized) — high priority for Optimize recommendations.
- Reranking: plan hybrid flow — lightweight dual-encoder for recall then cross-encoder rerank for precision on top 50. Want Redwood to support model routing (cheaper CPU rerank fallback).
- Embedding model: prefer open/TF-compatible embeddings (open models) but open to using hosted embeddings for latency. Must support switching model variants without re-indexing (vector refresh policy).

Vector DB / connector requirements called out explicitly:
- Must support bulk import with resume + streaming upserts (near real-time ingestion < 2s visibility).
- Hybrid search: filter by metadata (date, client_id, compliance_flags) AND vector similarity in same query.
- Namespace / multi-tenant isolation for per-business-unit indices.
- Support HNSW/OPQ/quantization configs and ability to export/import shards.
- API: robust REST + SDKs (python), and server-side async job status endpoints.
- Security: private endpoints/VPC peering, TLS mTLS, data encryption-at-rest, KMS integration, fine-grained RBAC.
- Observability: per-index metrics (qps, recall, index_size), query trace ids, and ability to attach to Redwood Console for token-level cost.
- Backup/restore and snapshot scheduling (for legal e-discovery).

Preferred integrations under consideration: Pinecone (managed performance), pgvector (postgres-based for strong filtering), Weaviate (schema + modules) and Elastic (hybrid search + familiarity in infra). Need a clear connector matrix from Redwood showing feature parity (esp. streaming upserts, TTL, hybrid filters).
